summary: Scholarship for international students who completed a first degree abroad and want to do a master's or PhD in Germany. Priority goes to applicants from DAC countries who have not yet moved to Germany.
deadlineNote: Spring 2027 round: 15 January to 1 March 2027. Next round 15 July to 1 September 2027.
name: Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarship for International Graduate and PhD Students
covers: scholarship support (amount not stated on the page)
eligibilityNotes: Priority (not an exclusive rule) for applicants from DAC countries, i.e. developing countries; the page does not list the countries. Applicants should still be outside Germany when applying. Master's applicants need a completed first degree abroad; PhD applicants a completed graduate degree abroad. Stipend amount not given on the page.

summary: Three-year doctoral scholarship for foreign PhD students living in Germany for study or research, with seminars and political education events. Selection looks at academic quality and social and political engagement.
deadlineNote: Deadline is 1 October for grants starting 1 April the next year; the 2026 deadline has passed.
name: Rosa Luxemburg Foundation Doctoral Scholarship (international PhD students)
eligibilityNotes: Page says it funds domestic and foreign PhD students; no nationality list. International grants go to PhD students temporarily living in Germany for study or research, accepted at a German university. German at B2 or higher is a selection criterion; application materials are German only. Medicine, dentistry and veterinary medicine are not eligible. Stipend amount not stated.

summary: Monthly stipend for foreign doctoral candidates admitted to a doctorate at a German university, for all subjects except medicine. Typically runs three and a half years.
deadlineNote: No fixed dates on the page; apply once admitted to a doctorate and no later than two years before the dissertation ends.
name: Friedrich Ebert Foundation PhD Funding for Foreign Doctoral Candidates
eligibilityNotes: FES FAQ: for students and doctoral candidates from the global South (Asia, Africa, Latin America), former CIS states and eastern and south-eastern EU states; OECD states such as the USA, Australia, New Zealand and Japan are excluded. Country list expanded to codes by us, so borderline countries may differ. Applicants must be abroad or in Germany no more than 15 months (limit does not apply to those who came to study or research). Stipend EUR 1,500/month (amount = x12). Very good German (B2 accepted) required even for English dissertations; medicine excluded.

summary: Monthly stipend for foreign bachelor and master students enrolled at German universities, with health insurance costs covered and seminars and mentoring. German language (B2) is required.
deadlineNote: Master's applicants: by 30 November for winter semester, 31 May for summer semester (year not stated on the page). Bachelor applicants apply after the first semester with no fixed date.
name: Friedrich Ebert Foundation Basic Funding for Foreign Students
eligibilityNotes: FES FAQ: for students from the global South (Asia, Africa, Latin America), former CIS states and eastern and south-eastern EU states; OECD states such as the USA, Australia, New Zealand and Japan excluded. Country list expanded to codes by us, so borderline countries may differ. Applicants must be abroad or in Germany no more than 15 months (limit does not apply to those who came to study). Stipend EUR 992/month (amount = x12). German B2 required even for English-taught programmes; social or political engagement expected. Bachelor: apply after 1st semester up to three semesters before the end of regular study time.

summary: Doctoral scholarship for PhD candidates admitted at a German university, including those with a foreign degree. Applicants are expected to belong to a Protestant church, with exceptions in justified cases.
deadlineNote: Window 1 September to the first business day in December (1 December 2026). Second window 1 March to first business day in June; EUR 12 processing fee.
name: Evangelisches Studienwerk Villigst Doctoral Scholarship
eligibilityNotes: No nationality or residence rule on the page; foreign-degree holders can apply once a German university has admitted them. Protestant church membership expected (exceptions justified individually). Stipend EUR 1,750/month (amount = x12) plus EUR 100/month research allowance. German B2 or DSH certificate required for non-German speakers. Funded 3 years, extendable to 4.5; not for dissertations in the final phase.

summary: Postgraduate scholarship for people from developing and emerging countries who want to do a master's, PhD or other postgraduate study in Germany. Applicants should be Catholic or proposed by Catholic partners.
deadlineNote: Page gives no dates; see the online application page or contact KAAD.
name: KAAD Scholarship Programme 1 (applicants from abroad)
covers: scholarship (amounts and coverage not stated on the page)
eligibilityNotes: Page says applicants must come from and currently live in a developing or emerging country in Africa, Asia, the Middle East or Latin America (other countries only in exceptional cases); no country list, so the code list is our expansion and borderline countries may differ. Needs a university degree and professional experience in the home country; German at least B1 (A2 for English-taught programmes) before entry. Applicants should be Catholic; other faiths can be funded if proposed by Catholic partners. Residence in an eligible country is required at application. Stipend not stated.

summary: Scholarship for students from Africa, Asia, the Middle East and Latin America who study or are about to start a master's or doctorate at a German university. Applications go through the university's Catholic student community.
deadlineNote: Selection committee meets twice a year; dates are not on the page, ask your KHG or KSG.
name: KAAD Scholarship Programme 2 (students already in Germany)
covers: scholarship (amounts not stated on the page)
eligibilityNotes: Page says applicants must come from a country in Africa, Asia, the Near and Middle East or Latin America; code list is our expansion. Must have been in Germany no more than 15 months, hold a study residence permit, and have at least six months of studies left. Catholic or other Christian; other faiths if nominated by Catholic partners. Apply via the university's KHG or KSG, not directly. Conversational German needed.

summary: Merit scholarship of EUR 1,000 a month for new bachelor's and master's students in maths, computer science, natural sciences and technology at Heidelberg. Open to applicants from Germany and abroad.
deadlineNote: Application window 15 May to 31 July each year; the 2026 window has passed, next one expected from 15 May 2027.
name: Hans-Peter Wild Talent Scholarships
eligibilityNotes: Open to students from Germany and abroad. MINT subject must be at least 50% of the course; applicant must be starting their first semester at Heidelberg and be enrolled (separate admission application needed). Stipend EUR 1,000/month (amount = x12). First funding period two semesters, ideally supported to the end of studies.

summary: Bavarian state-funded scholarship for international degree students and doctoral candidates at LMU, based on academic excellence and financial need.
deadlineNote: Last listed window 15 January to 8 March 2026 has passed; next round not yet published.
name: SIST LMU Study Scholarship
eligibilityNotes: For international students and doctoral candidates in regular full-time programmes at LMU; German nationals are not covered (excluded code is our reading of 'international'). Needs academic excellence, subject knowledge and financial need.

summary: DAAD-funded scholarship for international bachelor's, master's and state-exam students at Bonn who expect to graduate within 12 months and have good grades.
deadlineNote: 2026 selection is complete; next call expected in December 2026, subject to funding.
name: University of Bonn Degree Completion Scholarship
eligibilityNotes: Regular enrolment at Bonn (not exchange students), non-German citizenship (dual nationals with German citizenship excluded), university entrance qualification gained outside Germany, grade average of at least 2.5, graduation expected within 12 months.

summary: DAAD-funded support of EUR 650 a month for five months for international students at Bonn with a refugee background, disability or chronic illness, or caring duties.
deadlineNote: Last listed deadline 15 June 2025 has passed; the current round is not published on the page.
name: University of Bonn Equal Opportunity Scholarship
eligibilityNotes: Regular enrolment at Bonn, non-German citizenship (dual German excluded), foreign entrance qualification, plus at least one of: refugee background, disability of 50% or more or chronic condition, caring for a child under 18 or a close relative. Amount is EUR 650 x 5 months, per the 2025 round.

summary: DAAD-funded support of EUR 650 a month for five months for international Bonn students with good grades and at least six months of exceptional voluntary work.
deadlineNote: Last listed deadline 15 June 2025 has passed; the current round is not published on the page.
name: University of Bonn Exceptional Engagement Scholarship
eligibilityNotes: Regular enrolment at Bonn, non-German citizenship (dual German excluded), foreign entrance qualification, at least the second programme-related semester, good to very good grades and six months of exceptional voluntary work. Amount is EUR 650 x 5 months, per the 2025 round.

summary: Need-based support for bachelor's students (including international applicants) who face a disadvantaged start or financial hardship. The committee sets each amount from the student's stated monthly need.
deadlineNote: 2026 windows closed (current students 27 April-1 June, bachelor's applicants 10 June-15 July 2026).
name: Opportunity Mannheim Scholarship
covers: monthly need-based funding, up to one year
eligibilityNotes: German citizenship not required; applicants must be enrolled in or have applied for a bachelor's programme at Mannheim (page also lists current master's students; master's applicants are excluded). Fall semester only. No fixed amount; funding up to one year, reapplication possible.
